Abstract
We confront the universal path-contour master-functional formulation of the Unified Phase Dynamics (UPD) with recent landmark laboratory measurements testing the quantum Equivalence Principle on an atom chip ("Quantum Galileo Interferometer", Science Advances, 2024). In the experiment, an atomic wave packet of $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$ is coherently split into a spatially held branch and a freely falling branch, accumulating a measurable cubic phase shift of $\Delta\Phi pprox 80.0\ \mathrm{rad}$ over an interrogation time of $T = 1.22\ \mathrm{ms}$ with spatial separation $\Delta z pprox 7.30\ \mu\mathrm{m}$. We rigorously deduce this cubic phase evolution directly from the action differential of the UPD master-functional $\mathbf{\Psi}[\Sigma]$, obtaining $\Delta\Phi_{\mathrm{UPD}} = rac{m g^2 T^3}{3\hbar} = 80.0\ \mathrm{rad}$, matching the empirical observation with sub-percent accuracy. Furthermore, we address the critical question of why atomic interferometers exhibit unperturbed quantum coherence with near-unity fringe visibility, in contrast to macroscopic classical trajectories. Computing the non-perturbative gravitational path decoherence rate $\Gamma_{\mathrm{UPD}}(M) = rac{6 G M^2}{5 \hbar r_{\mathrm{loc}}}$ governed by the master-functional localization radius $r_{\mathrm{loc}} = 2.05 imes 10^{-13}\ \mathrm{m}$, we establish that for $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$ ($M = 1.44 imes 10^{-25}\ \mathrm{kg}$), the gravitational decoherence lifetime is $ au_{\mathrm{UPD}} pprox 4.11 imes 10^5\ \mathrm{years}$, yielding a spontaneous collapse probability of merely $P pprox 9.4 imes 10^{-17}$ over the experimental cycle. We demonstrate that the quantum-to-classical transition is governed by a strict quadratic mass-scaling law ($\Gamma \propto M^2$), remaining completely unobservable in atomic systems but predicting decisive gravitational decoherence ($ au_{\mathrm{crit}} pprox 10\ \mathrm{ms}$) at the mesoscopic threshold $M_{\mathrm{crit}} pprox 3.13 imes 10^{12}\ \mathrm{amu}$ ($R = 81.1\ \mathrm{nm}$ silicon nanosphere) accessible in Experimentum Crucis 1.

1. Introduction and Experimental Context

The interface between quantum mechanics and general relativity represents one of the most profound frontiers of contemporary fundamental physics. While standard quantum field theory treats gravity as an external classical background or an unrenormalizable gauge interaction, real-world laboratory tests have increasingly pushed into the quantum regime where gravitational fields actively modulate quantum wave functions.

In September 2024, a landmark experiment conducted by an international consortium was published in Science Advances under the title "Quantum Galileo: Testing the equivalence principle with a single atom on an atom chip". Utilizing state-of-the-art atom-chip magnetic microtraps, the team realized a true quantum realization of Galileo's experiment: a single coherent wave packet of $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$ is split into two quantum paths: one held stationary, and one in free fall.

2. Deductive Derivation of the Cubic Phase Shift in Unified Phase Dynamics

In Unified Phase Dynamics, the gravitational action along the contour master-functional yields: $$\Delta\Phi_{\mathrm{UPD}}(T) = rac{1}{\hbar} \int_0^T \left[ \Delta E_{\mathrm{kin}}(t) - \Delta V_{\mathrm{grav}}(t) ight] dt = rac{m g^2 T^3}{3\hbar}.$$ For $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$ with $m = 1.443 imes 10^{-25}\ \mathrm{kg}$, $g = 9.80665\ \mathrm{m/s}^2$, and $T = 1.22 imes 10^{-3}\ \mathrm{s}$: $$\Delta\Phi_{\mathrm{UPD}} = \mathbf{79.98\ \mathrm{rad}} pprox \mathbf{80.0\ \mathrm{rad}}.$$ This analytical derivation perfectly reproduces the measured phase shift without any free or adjustable parameters.

3. Resolution of the Coherence Paradox: Quadratic Mass Scaling

The non-perturbative gravitational decoherence rate is: $$\Gamma_{\mathrm{UPD}}(M) = rac{6 G M^2}{5 \hbar r_{\mathrm{loc}}},$$ where $r_{\mathrm{loc}} = 2.05 imes 10^{-13}\ \mathrm{m}$. For $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$: $$\Gamma_{\mathrm{UPD}} = 7.72 imes 10^{-14}\ \mathrm{s}^{-1} \implies au_{\mathrm{UPD}} = 4.11 imes 10^5\ \mathrm{years}.$$ The spontaneous collapse probability over the interrogation time $T = 1.22\ \mathrm{ms}$ is: $$P_{\mathrm{collapse}} = 1 - e^{-\Gamma T} pprox 9.4 imes 10^{-17}.$$ This explains why atom interferometry exhibits pristine, near-unity fringe visibility ($V pprox 0.98$), while macroscopic bodies undergo instantaneous gravitational decoherence.
